kept.q: A solution that contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a given quantity of solvent at a particular temperature, with undissolved solute still present at the bottom, is called a/an:
kept.explanation: A saturated solution holds the maximum solute possible at that temperature, so any extra solute stays undissolved at the bottom. This is different from a dilute or unsaturated solution, which can still dissolve more solute.
kept.pidgin: Saturated solution na solution wey don carry the maximum solute wey e fit carry for that temperature, so any extra solute go remain for ground. E different from dilute or unsaturated solution wey still fit dissolve more solute.

kept.q: A village stream in Enugu State contains dissolved calcium hydrogencarbonate, causing temporary hardness. Which method will most effectively remove this type of hardness?
options: Adding common salt to the water
Dissolving more calcium hydrogencarbonate in it
kept.explanation: Boiling decomposes calcium hydrogencarbonate into insoluble calcium carbonate, carbon dioxide and water, removing the hardness. Filtering only removes solid particles, while adding salt or more hardness-causing substance does not remove hardness.
kept.pidgin: If you boil the water, the calcium hydrogencarbonate go break down to calcium carbonate (wey no dey dissolve), CO2 and water, so the hardness go comot. Filtering na only for solid particles, e no fit remove dissolved hardness.

kept.q: At 45°C, 25 g of sodium chloride dissolves completely in 50 g of water to form a saturated solution. What is the solubility of sodium chloride at this temperature, expressed in grams per 100 g of water?
kept.explanation: Solubility is usually expressed per 100 g of water. Since 25 g dissolves in 50 g of water, scaling up (multiply by 2) gives 50 g dissolving in 100 g of water, so the solubility is 50 g/100 g of water.
kept.pidgin: Dem dey measure solubility per 100 g of water. Since 25 g dissolve for 50 g water, if you double am (times 2), e go be 50 g wey go dissolve for 100 g water. So solubility na 50 g/100 g water.

kept.q: The solubility of potassium trioxonitrate(V), KNO3, in water at 60°C is 110 g per 100 g of water. What mass of KNO3 is required to just saturate 250 g of water at this temperature?
kept.explanation: Solubility of 110 g per 100 g of water means for 250 g of water, you multiply 110 by (250/100) = 2.5. This gives 110 x 2.5 = 275 g of KNO3 needed to saturate the water.
kept.pidgin: Solubility na 110 g per 100 g water, so for 250 g water, you go multiply 110 by (250/100) wey be 2.5. 110 x 2.5 go give you 275 g KNO3 wey go saturate the water.

kept.q: The solubility of a salt X is 90 g per 100 g of water at 90°C and 30 g per 100 g of water at 10°C. A saturated solution of X is prepared using 400 g of water at 90°C and then slowly cooled to 10°C without any loss of water by evaporation. Calculate the mass of crystals of X that will separate out on cooling.
kept.explanation: At 90°C, mass dissolved in 400 g water = (90/100) x 400 = 360 g. At 10°C, only (30/100) x 400 = 120 g can stay dissolved. The excess that crystallises out = 360 g - 120 g = 240 g.
kept.pidgin: For 90°C, the mass wey dissolve for 400 g water na (90/100) x 400 = 360 g. For 10°C, na only (30/100) x 400 = 120 g fit still dissolve. So the extra wey go turn to crystal na 360 g - 120 g = 240 g.

kept.q: Which of the following correctly describes how the solubility of a gas such as carbon(IV) oxide in water is affected by changes in temperature and pressure?
options: It is independent of temperature and pressure
It decreases with an increase in pressure
It increases with an increase in temperature
It increases with an increase in pressure
kept.explanation: Gas solubility in a liquid increases as the pressure of the gas above the liquid increases, as stated by Henry's Law, and it decreases as temperature rises because the gas molecules gain energy and escape more easily. So the correct behaviour is that solubility increases with increased pressure.
kept.pidgin: Gas dey more soluble for water as the pressure wey dey push the gas enter the liquid dey increase (na so Henry's Law talk am), but e dey less soluble as temperature dey rise because the gas molecules go get more energy make dem waka comot. So the correct one be say solubility dey increase as pressure dey increase.
